objects.name: CTFT Project
objects.description: Capture-The-Flag Techniques - an ontology of CTF solving behaviour. Relates to MITRE ATT&CK, CAPEC and CWE as per-entry anchors; not a parallel ATT&CK. Generalized from FOM.

objects.name: Full Pwn / Multi-Stage
objects.description: Challenges that require a complete host or infrastructure compromise across multiple stages — reconnaissance, foothold, and privilege escalation — before the flag is reachable. The flag is reachable only at the end of the chain, so no single technique solves the challenge. (HTB: Fullpwn)

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-001 - Multi-stage chained challenge
objects.description: The flag(s) require a full host compromise: external reconnaissance, initial foothold, and privilege escalation — each gate concealed by a separate vulnerability or design decision.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-001 - Chain enumeration, foothold and privilege escalation
objects.description: Run port and service enumeration, exploit the exposed service for a foothold, then run local enumeration scripts (linpeas/winpeas) to identify the privilege-escalation path. Chain each stage methodically until the root/administrator flag is reached.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-002 - Windows Active Directory fullpwn
objects.description: The flag resides on a Domain Controller; reaching it requires a chain of AD-specific attacks (Kerberoasting, AS-REP Roasting, delegation abuse, or ACL exploitation) rather than a single CVE.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-002 - Enumerate AD, abuse delegation or ACL paths to the DC
objects.description: Run BloodHound/SharpHound to map the AD graph; identify shortest attack paths (Kerberoastable service accounts, ACL GenericWrite, unconstrained delegation). Follow the path: crack the hash → lateral movement → DCSync or SeBackupPrivilege to dump NTDS.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-003 - Multi-hop network pivot
objects.description: The flag host sits on a network segment not directly reachable from the attacker; reaching it requires traversing one or more intermediate compromised hosts via tunnelling or proxying.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-003 - Tunnel through compromised hosts to reach the flag
objects.description: Deploy a lightweight SOCKS5 tunnel (chisel server/client) or SSH dynamic-forward through each compromised host; chain proxychains to route all tool traffic through the tunnel stack until the flag host is reachable.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-004 - Container / service misconfiguration chain
objects.description: The flag requires chaining a service-level misconfiguration (weak credentials, exposed API, SSRF) with a container-escape technique to break out to the host filesystem.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-004 - Chain service misconfig and container escape to host
objects.description: Exploit the exposed service (weak credentials, SSRF, command injection) to gain container-level execution, then apply the appropriate container-escape technique (privileged mode, socket mount, writable host path) to reach the host flag.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-005 - Cloud-integrated fullpwn
objects.description: The flag is stored in a cloud resource (S3 bucket, Secrets Manager, Lambda environment variable) that is reachable only after compromising an on-premises host and pivoting through its attached cloud credentials.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-005 - Pivot from on-prem to cloud IAM to retrieve the secret
objects.description: After gaining on-premises access, query the cloud instance metadata endpoint (e.g. 169.254.169.254) for IAM role credentials, enumerate the role's permissions with aws iam, and retrieve the flag from the authorised cloud resource (S3, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store).
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-006 - Chained database trust-context escalation
objects.description: Several declared database services trust one another with different execution contexts. A low-privilege entry can traverse a chain whose effective identity has more privileges than the initial identity. The challenge models the trust relation and privilege boundary; it does not embed a query or credential.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-006 - Map database trust contexts and privilege boundaries
objects.description: Build a graph from the challenge's declared service links and redacted identity observations. Rank only paths whose trust edge, effective context and target privilege boundary are all evidenced.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-007 - Uninventoried dual-stack management path
objects.description: A management service is declared on an address family absent from the primary inventory. The challenge requires reconciling interface records, service binds and access policy before treating the alternate route as a possible path.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-007 - Reconcile dual-stack management exposure
objects.description: Compare the supplied interface inventory, service binds and policy declarations. Create a candidate route only when all three name the same authorized challenge asset and access boundary.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-008 - Linux local privesc chain (SUID, ACLs, sudo, capabilities)
objects.description: The flag is root-only; escalation requires chaining SUID binaries, ACLs, sudo rules or capabilities.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-008 - Enumerate and chain Linux privesc vectors
objects.description: Enumerate privesc vectors (linpeas), exploit one or chain several, and read the flag.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-009 - Redis/NoSQL service misconfiguration chain
objects.description: An internal DB service is misconfigured (no auth, weak credentials); the flag is in the data or reachable via RCE.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-009 - Enumerate Redis/Mongo/MySQL, dump or RCE
objects.description: Enumerate the service, dump data or achieve code execution, and pivot to the flag.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-010 - Reverse-shell delivery & listener operations
objects.description: The flag requires a stable reverse shell through restricted channels (firewalls, encodings).

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-010 - Catch, upgrade and persist reverse shells
objects.description: Deliver a reverse shell (bash/python/php), catch it with a listener, upgrade to a PTY, and persist.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-011 - Alternate key-credential backdoor on a machine account
objects.description: A domain user is granted GenericWrite over a computer account, but the classic exploitation path (create a fake machine then abuse delegation) is closed by a zero Machine Account Quota. The intended move is to attach an alternate key credential (msDS-KeyCredentialLink) to the computer object and authenticate with the generated certificate, without ever changing the account's password.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-011 - Detect and revoke key-credential backdoors
objects.description: Confirm the write edge on the computer object, then attach a key credential to it and request a TGT through PKINIT. Derive the NT hash from the PAC. If one collection tool reports no interesting path, re-collect the graph with a second collector and compare coverage before giving up.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-012 - Certificate-derived Kerberos authentication chain
objects.description: The planted or stolen certificate is useless to ordinary password-based tooling. The solver must chain PKINIT authentication (pass the certificate) into a TGT, then extract the account's NT hash from the PAC of the ticket (unPAC the hash) before standard Kerberos and NTLM moves unlock the next hop.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-012 - Validate PKINIT trust and extract PAC material
objects.description: Load the PFX with its export password and request a TGT for the backdoored account. Keep the AS-REP encryption key printed by the exchange, then extract the NT hash from the PAC of the ticket and switch to hash-based tooling.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-013 - Certificate template reconfiguration for arbitrary enrollment
objects.description: A domain user holds WriteDacl over a certificate template. The path is invisible to basic user and share enumeration: it lives in ADCS template ACLs, and only a graph-aware collection reveals it. The solver reconfigures the template (ESC4), enrolls a certificate for an arbitrary identity, and authenticates with it.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-013 - Lock down certificate template ACLs and enrollment
objects.description: Enumerate ADCS with a certificate-aware scanner and list templates whose ACLs allow a controlled account to write. Reconfigure the target template, request a certificate with the desired UPN, then authenticate with the certificate to obtain a TGT or recover the account hash.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-014 - Injection through a delegated session configuration
objects.description: The box is only reachable through a constrained delegation endpoint (JEA) backed by a custom module. A module parameter is concatenated unsafely into a command, so the endpoint becomes an injection gate. The module source itself is distributed through a shared scripts folder, making the review step part of the challenge.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-014 - Constrain delegated endpoints and log session commands
objects.description: Enumerate startup scripts and shared folders for the constrained endpoint's module source. Audit each module for parameters concatenated into commands, inject through the unsafe parameter to execute commands as the delegated principal, and plant a local persistence account before leaving the endpoint.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-015 - Default database credential enabling command execution
objects.description: A server exposes an MSSQL instance whose sa account still uses a default password. The only hint is buried in a service account's description text. Once the credential is guessed, the solver escalates through xpcmdshell, which the author left enabled, to run commands as the SQL service account.

external_references.description: Server Software Component: SQL Stored Procedures

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-015 - Enumerate database defaults and disable dangerous procedures
objects.description: Read account descriptions for password hints, then brute force the database admin account with default-credential wordlists. Once authenticated, enable or abuse xpcmdshell to execute operating-system commands as the service account and inspect its privileges.

external_references.description: Server Software Component: SQL Stored Procedures

objects.description: Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-016 - Packed token-impersonation binary evading endpoint defenses
objects.description: The SQL service account holds SeImpersonatePrivilege, the classic potato-class escalation, but endpoint protection is running and known binaries are blocked. The solver must repackage the impersonation binary with a packer so it clears static detection, deliver it over HTTP, and abuse the privileged token to reach SYSTEM.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-016 - Audit privileged tokens and unpack suspicious binaries
objects.description: Enumerate the current account's privileges; when SeImpersonatePrivilege is present, deliver an impersonation binary to the target. If endpoint protection blocks it, repackage the binary with a packer, serve it over HTTP, and execute it to run commands as SYSTEM and plant a local account.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-017 - Coerced domain controller authentication toward a delegated host
objects.description: A compromised server is configured with unconstrained delegation: any ticket sent to it is cached locally. The author expects the solver to monitor incoming authentication on that server while coercing the domain controller to connect, capturing the DC machine ticket. A case-sensitivity detail in the coercion hostname is the hidden obstacle.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-017 - Constrain delegation trust and detect coerced authentication
objects.description: Start a ticket monitor on the delegated host targeting the domain controller machine account, then trigger the printer-bug coercion with the exact hostname casing. Capture the DC machine ticket, request a service ticket with it, and use the resulting access to dump the domain controller.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-018 - Cross-domain credential reuse after hidden-namespace discovery
objects.description: A second domain is never mentioned in the scope handout: it surfaces only in a hosts entry on the first domain controller. The author reuses one account name and password across both domains, so the solver must discover the hidden namespace, map its network records, and replay the harvested credentials.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-018 - Map adjacent namespaces and test credential reuse
objects.description: Read hosts entries and DNS zone records on a compromised host to find adjacent namespaces, enumerate their network records, and replay every harvested credential against the new domain. Re-run the graph collection on the second domain before planning the next stage.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-019 - Interactive-shell history and protected credential stores
objects.description: The next credentials are not exposed by any service: they sit in the administrator's PowerShell readline history and inside DPAPI-protected scheduled task blobs. The author expects credential archaeology on the first host instead of network exploitation for the next hop.

external_references.description: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-019 - Harvest shell histories and decrypt protected stores
objects.description: Read the console history file of the administrator profile for typed credentials, then dump DPAPI masterkeys and credential blobs with local administrative rights. Search the decrypted material for domain accounts and their passwords to fuel the next hop.

external_references.description: Credentials from Password Stores: Windows Credential Manager

objects.description: Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FPN-020 - Flag payload embedded in directory object properties
objects.description: The final flag is not a file on any host: it is stored in a property of a directory object, reachable only by dumping the whole domain and searching the serialized attributes. Host compromise alone returns nothing; directory-level exfiltration is the required final stage.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FPN-020 - Dump directory attributes and search hidden payloads
objects.description: After domain compromise, dump the directory into serialized artifacts and search every field case-insensitively for the flag format. When no flag file exists on any host, treat directory attributes as the payload location.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique. `mitigates` is kept for STIX-consumer compatibility; the CTFT semantics are carried by x_ctft_relation.
